Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

18:4973-1968 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
BADMINTON WOOLLEN BALLS 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Insti- 
tution on 30 December 1968, after the draft finalized by the Sports 
Goods Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consumer 
Products Division Council. 

0.2 Ball badminton is a widely-played game. As the performance of a 
team or player is dependent to a large extent on the equipment he 
uses and the equipment that is made available in competitions, formula- 
tion of this standard was considered essential. 

0.3 This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards on sports goods, 
prepared on the recommendations of the Sports Goods Export Promotion 
Council, New Delhi. 

0.4 In the formulation of this standard, assistance has been derived 

from the * Rules of games and sports*, Ed 16 YMCA Publishing House, 

Calcutta. 

0.5 Clause 7.1 calls for an agreement between the purchaser and the 

supplier or permits the purchaser to use his option for selection to suit his 

requirements, 

0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of 

this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, 

expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with 

IS : 2 - 1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded 

off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this 

standard. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard lays down material, dimensional and manufacturing 
requirements of badminton woollen balls. 



*KiiIe8 far rounding off numerical values ( revised )• 

3 



15:4973-1968 

2. MATERIAL 

2.1 Fine woollen thread, pale or dark-yellow in colour and free from 
foreign matter shall be used for the manufacture of woollen balls. 

3. DIAMETER AND WEIGHT 

3pl The diameter and weight of the ball shall be as specified below: 

Diameter, mm 54'0 Max 

50-8 Min 

Weight, g 14-58 Max 

1312 Min 

4. MANUFACTURE, WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

4.1 The manufacturing portion starts with cutting the woollen threads 
to suitable lengths required. These cut threads are then taken together 
in fours and wound round a set of blades consisting of two parts. After 
the winding is over, the two blades are fixed together to form a circle 
and a pin fitted into the insertions to prevent the wound up half finished 
balls from loosening out. In the next step the threads are cut in the 
middle along the outer periphery of the blades so that the blades open 
out in the reverse direction. At this stage a thicker thread ( hemp 
twine, cotton or synthetic ) is tied round in that direction to give a 
squeezed finish. The final process is to trim the opened up pieces of 
balls to the appropriate size. Any other process for manufacture of 
balls may be adopted but the woollen balls obtained in all cases shall 
be spherical in shape, free from broken ends, uneven spots and loose 
fibres. The spread of the wool shall be uniform in all the directions 
and the centre of gravity shall lie at the centre of the ball ( centre of 
gravity shall be determined by hanging the ball by a thread from 
various points and then plotting the lines and judging their inter- 
section ). 

5. PERFORMANCE 

5.1 When hit in a normal way by a player, the ball shall travel in its 
flight without wobble or spin. 

6. MARKING 

6.1 Each package of balls shall carry the manufacturer's name, 
identification mark or registered trade*inark. 

6*1.1 Each package of balls may also be marked with the ISI Certifi- 
cation Mark, 

NoTB — The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the 
Indian Standards Institution ( Certtficatlon MMxks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations 



iS:4973-t968 

made diereimder. The ISI Mark on produets covered by tm Indian* Standard 
conveys the assurance that they have been produced to com^y wilh the requirements 
ofthatstandardunder a w^Kidmedsys^in of inq>ectton, testing and quality control 
which is devised and si;^iervued by ISI and operated by the produco'. ISI soarked 
products are also continuoudy checked by ISI for cxmfmmity to diat standard as a 
further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of die ISI 
Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained 
ufom the Indian Standards Institution. 



7* PACKING 

7.1 The balls shall be packed as agreed ta between the purchaser and 
thesupplien
